results.notes: I wrote the code and tests for the whole slice. Nothing was run (code-first order). The guard's compile needs lead_todo items 1, 4 and 5 applied first: without them session-core's debug_assert on the ZDR feature key and the two MG MemoryService mocks break the build. Session-core gets the user_profiles table in migration 0100 (round B moves round A's 0072 to 0100-0104, and EP-8 S4 is the first of those; 0072 is taken here by space_event_log). The migration also widens the closed memory_control_events.event CHECK with 'profile_edited' and 'profile_rebuilt', so profile changes are audited without content. The revert file undoes both. user_profile.rs holds the pure builder: stated rows, then unknown-provenance rows, then inferred rows at confidence 0.8 or more; one line per key and per text; ordered preference, fact, instruction; cut at 1400 characters on a line boundary. The loader reads session-core agent_memory scope='user' rows only: accepted, latest, unexpired, session_id NULL, source_links <> '{}', legacy Space-room rows excluded. It never reads Letta blocks (C8). It also has rebuild (under the user lock through resolve_in_tx; refused unless generation_allowed; an edited profile is kept unless force; writes nothing when unchanged), save_edit (allowed while paused, refused when hidden, revision checked under the lock), drop_sources and delete_in_tx. The three MemoryService RPCs are in memory_grpc.rs, behind a profile_enabled field read once from SESSION_USER_PROFILE_ENABLED with the strict parser. With the switch off they return failed_precondition profile_not_enabled after authorization and before any DB read. A ZDR Get answers empty with skip_reason=zdr. ZDR and waived Set/Rebuild get Refusal::feature_not_supported("user_profile"). Erasure is not switched: a memory delete drops its built line in the same transaction, ResetMemory deletes the row, and the org purge deletes the org's rows (PurgeSummary.user_profiles). The end of each Dreaming cycle rebuilds, without force, for each person whose user rows the cycle wrote; that list stays empty while the switch is off. The model-gateway routes are GET/PUT /v1/memories/profile and POST /v1/memories/profile/rebuild, with org and user taken from the claims. The BFF proxies /api/v1/memory/profile and /api/v1/memory/profile/rebuild. The SPA has getProfile, saveProfile and rebuildProfile, the actions memory.profile.save and memory.profile.rebuild (both exempt, human-only), and a Profile card above the memory list. The card is hidden on profile_not_enabled or a 404, so the existing MemorySection tests keep their output. It has a textarea with a 1400-character counter, 'Bygd fra N minner' with each line linking to #memory-<id>, the count of deleted sources for an edited profile, and the paused/off/ZDR states per D8. The evidence stub is in docs/plans/wave3/evidence/EP-8-S4.md.

depth_findings.text: No live proof yet: the design's F3 (one three-query call, a fetch_url by ref, Quarry edge logs showing three searches, and round count against the switch off) must run before MODEL_GATEWAY_WEB_SEARCH_BATCH is turned on.

The relevance gate judges a batch against its queries joined into one question (searched_question), so a hit that answers one query can be set aside for missing the other queries' terms; check kept counts on a live batch before switch-on.

Refs are issued to every merged hit, including hits the gate later sets aside, and they are sequential, so a model can guess an unshown ref (w5 after w4) and fetch a set-aside page; only refs shown in the gated text should resolve.

The merge drops hits beyond eight without saying so, and the gate's 'found' count is the capped number, so the model cannot see that hits were cut; the gated header should state the cap when it applies.

Forced pre-loop searches (run_forced_web_search and run_forced_web_search_for_model, called from sse.rs) issue no refs, so their hits show no [wN] label; threading the turn's refs needs an sse.rs change, and EP-7-S3 owns sse.rs in this batch.
A batch fails whole when one query fails, discarding hits Quarry already returned and billed; a visible partial-result note would need a new field in gated_web_search_output.
'ref' now names a search ref (w2) in fetch_url and a parked-result handle (res_...) in read_page and find_in_page; the same word in one schema invites mixing them, so rename one before switch-on.
Refs live per process, so a turn resumed on another replica gets 'was not issued' for every ref; this fails closed but is untested (design risk 5).
Nothing caps provider calls beyond the schema text and the four-query check; each batch is up to four billed Quarry searches (D2-321), so the live proof must record search counts per round.
The new ZDR row proves the posture only; the batched refusal rests on the existing browse_web to web_search refusal in tests/zdr_feature_table.rs, which does not name batched calls.
No test proves the scheduled lane never offers or accepts 'queries'; the lane sits outside this loop (execution-core scheduled_agent.rs), so a contract test there belongs in a later slice.
rerank_report_of reads only the first merged item's rerank status, so the coverage line disappears when the first hit came from an unreranked query.
advertise_batched_search restates the web_search and fetch_url parameter schemas as text beside the literal definitions, so a later edit to one must be repeated in the other.
TurnRefs has no cap; it grows by at most eight entries per search call and is dropped with the turn.
